You know, it's just probably me playing devil's advocate as I like to do, but there's a part of me that wants to be against this, because developers/publishers shouldn't have the power to control the media as the media is meant for the people. To an extent, the media SHOULD be expected to make leaks that developers should be absolutely afraid of as sometimes those leaks help serve the public (like say leaking out the terms that were behind the Shadow of Mordor stuff, regardless as to if the game was good or bad those terms were horrible for the consumer) and when they do serve the public those outlets should at least be resilient to any backlash that the publishers/developers might have... But every time I go down this train of thought, every time I try to argue these companies shouldn't have this sort of power over the games media, every damn time the counter-point I come up with is, "Well, it's Kotaku, they have not been serving the gaming consumer for awhile." I may not like the idea of developers or publishers being able to blacklist the media but that's only to help the consumer, in cases like this where the issue seems to be that the outlet was harming the consumers (alpha states always have bugs, point that out only serves to direct the time/energy of a consumer to avoid a product that might have none of these issues on release while making it more difficult for devs who potentially put out a good product to give consumers more of what they want...) I have a hard time feeling sympathy. If they want to get the benefits of having articles/blog posts out about a game as the game is released then they need to hold up their share of the situation and inform the consumer, or at LEAST shill out the company.

Seriously, it seems like Kotaku is biting BOTH the hands that feed it (at least when it comes to gaming), the companies that give them special previews to get their stuff up early as well as the consumer base which they get those special previews to inform to! If you want to be apart of this game you should at LEAST stand with one side of the supply/demand chart.... Er.... One of the influential sides I guess (rather than trying to boost up their friends who made games or maybe trying to have the casual market interested in following 'gaming' news)

But those are just my thoughts.

While it does bode ill for a publisher to be able to control the media so much, I think the problem with Kotaku was the NDA agreement they were legally bound to adhere to. They weren't doing it. It's not necessary to get a game early in order to review it, and since they would not follow instructions, they had their privilege revoked. Even if they fear that buying a game will influence their opinion of it, there's ways to get around that. Maybe Kotaku as a company should begin budgeting for purchasing games, and that way the burden of cost won't influence their reviewers. Smaller gaming news sources get by just fine without special free copy privileges. I think it would actually be pretty healthy if things changed in the gaming industry, and the first week of release people were cautious of a game until reviews hit. Reviews that were not free to publications with NDAs and other things attached.

That's probably not going to happen, but still.
